title: MCCE: A Framework for Multi-LLM Collaborative Co-Evolution

mechanism.populationDetail: Section 4.1 maintains a pool \(P_t\) of molecules and forms \(P_{t+1}\) through Pareto-front survivor selection; no islands or maintained genealogy tree are described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; the Pareto-selected next-generation population is not a distinct archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: A separate trajectory dataset stores successful prompt-parent-candidate-score records for local-model training; it is experience memory, not an elite candidate archive.
mechanism.generationDetail: Two selected molecule parents are supplied together to the LLM operator, which produces two offspring candidates.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Successful prompt-parent-candidate-score trajectories are stored and later synthesized into DPO training pairs for local-model adaptation.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Section 4.1 gives tournament or fitness-proportional selection as examples but does not specify one fixed rule across runs.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/MCCE A Framework for Multi-LLM Collaborative Co-evolution.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Current multi-model prose can imply joint same-step generation, but MCCE describes alternating model invocations with indirect co-evolution. DPO preference pairs are training supervision, not preference-based primary evaluation. Exploration/exploitation roles are explicit but the operational alternation schedule is under-specified.
